## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)

- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)

## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

function wedgeGeo(w,h,l,opts){
 const geo=new THREE.BoxGeometry(w,h,l,1,1,1);
 const pos=geo.attributes.position;
 for(i...){let x=..., y=..., z=...;
   const t=(z+l/2)/l; // 0 front,1 rear
   if(y>0){ y-= opts.frontDrop*Math.pow(1-t,1.4); x*=opts.topFrontScale+(1-opts.topFrontScale)*t; }

   pos.setXYZ(i,x,y,z)

 geo.computeVertexNormals();
}

## Objective
- Build a 3D Knight Rider / K.I.T.T. game, requested "by unity engine", as a playable OMGithub web project with a matching Unity project included.

## Requirements
- User explicitly requested a 3D Knight Rider game made with Unity engine.
- Working environment serves a browser app on port 3002; Unity editor is unavailable, so a Three.js playable version is being built alongside a hand-authored Unity project.
- Support desktop and mobile browser gameplay with responsive UI/touch controls.
- Do not use the copyrighted Knight Rider theme; synth audio must be original.

## Decisions
- Deliver both: a polished browser-playable Three.js game as the runnable artifact, plus a Unity C#/scene project mirroring it.
- Use Vite + Three.js 0.169 with postprocessing bloom, ACES tone mapping, procedural car/environment geometry (no external models), canvas-generated textures, and synthesized WebAudio music/SFX.
- KITT is procedurally built from lofted geometry with red scanner, gold pinstripes, T-tops, taillights, spoiler, spoke wheels, headlights/spotlights and license plate.
- Gameplay: endless neon Nevada highway pursuit — collect data cores (+time), laser interceptors, dodge traffic, near-miss combo scoring, turbo boost, ramps/jumps, 120s timer, shields, rank/debrief.
- Added a title-only backdrop at +Z (mountains, sunset/moon, clouds, neon arch) because the attract camera looks back up the highway.
- Exposed `window.__game`, `window.__scene`, `window.__camera`, `window.__renderer`, and `window.__debugView` for testing.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created Vite/Three.js project and installed dependencies.
- Built full HUD/title/pause/game-over/mobile-control DOM and 80s neon CSS, including Orbitron/Rajdhani fonts.
- Implemented procedural KITT, traffic cars, interceptors, data cores, ramps, particles/explosions/lasers.
- Implemented full game loop: driving, turbo, steering, jumping, collisions, near misses, lasers, scoring/combo, shields, timer, difficulty, chase camera/menu orbit camera, game-over ranks.
- Implemented synthesized engine audio, scanner ping, music sequencer, laser/crash/pickup/boost/jump/game-over SFX.
- Implemented world: scrolling road texture, guardrails, streetlights, gantries/signs, overpasses, cacti, rocks, mountains, city, stars, moon, title backdrop.
- Fixed NaN wedge geometry (clamp `t`), fixed speedometer ring masking, fixed brake/tail glow orientation, fixed title stray "3D", reduced bloom blowouts, improved KITT body/cabin/wheels/lighting.
- Production build succeeds with `npx vite build --base ./`; title and gameplay screenshots render.

### Active
- Visual polish iteration: title composition and environment still need refinement; headlight bloom remains slightly blown out; KITT still reads somewhat boxy/pickup-like from some angles.
- Traffic/enemy wheels are unoptimized (~1100 meshes total, heavy draw calls).
- Unity project has not been created yet.

### Blocked
- Actual Unity editor/WebGL build is unavailable in this environment; Unity deliverable must be source-only.

## Next Move
1. Finish title-screen polish (car framing, scanner prominence, moon/clouds composition) and gameplay environment lighting.
2. Test active gameplay with simulated driving/firing, verify collisions, lasers, cores, ramps, pause, game over/restart, and mobile touch layout.
3. Optimize draw calls, especially traffic/enemy wheels (add simple 2–3-mesh wheel variant).
4. Re-run screenshots at desktop and mobile sizes, fix console errors, run `npm run build`.
5. Create `unity/` project: C# scripts (procedural KITT, controller, camera, world/traffic/spawning, weapons, HUD, synth audio, game manager), minimal scene + ProjectSettings + Packages manifest + `.meta` files, and README instructions.
6. Update `README.md` with controls, web/Unity instructions, and screenshots; commit changes.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: renderer/postprocessing, boot, UI wiring, input, HUD updates, debug hooks.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: all gameplay logic, pools, camera, scoring, spawns.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/car.js`: procedural KITT, traffic, enemies, cores, ramps, wheel/arch/loft helpers.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: sky, road, scrolling scenery, signs, title backdrop, lights.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/effects.js`: particle pool, explosions, shockwaves, laser beams.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: synthesized music/engine/SFX.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/textures.js`: canvas asphalt, signs, glow, moon, plate, clouds.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/style.css`: full UI/HUD/title/modal/touch/responsive styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: page structure and all screens/HUD DOM.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/package.json`: Vite + Three.js dependencies/scripts.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: visual iteration captures (`01-title.png` … `14-title.png`).
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/assets/fonts/`: vendored Orbitron and Rajdhani woff2 files.

## Important Context
- Vite dev server runs in tmux session `game` on `http://localhost:3002`: `npm run dev -- --port 3002`.
- `playwright-cli` needed `playwright-cli install-browser chromium`; screenshots use headed SwiftShader config.
- `window.__debugView = { pos:[x,y,z], look:[x,y,z], fov }` overrides camera each frame for inspection.

- Browser tests showed no console errors after fixes; gameplay screenshot shows working HUD, sign gantry, headlights, taillights.
- Git changes are uncommitted.

            Mesh mesh = Object.Instantiate(CubeTemplate());
            var verts = mesh.vertices;

                verts[i]=new Vector3(x,y,z);
            }
            mesh.vertices=verts; mesh.RecalculateNormals(); mesh.RecalculateBounds();
            return mesh;

public static class Mats {

 public static Material Standard(Color c, float metallic=0, float smooth=0.4f, Color? emission=null) {
   if (baseStandard == null) { baseStandard = Resources.Load<Material>("Materials/StandardBase"); }
   Material m;

   m.color=c; m.SetFloat("_Metallic",metallic); m.SetFloat("_Glossiness",smooth);

}

## Objective
- Build a 3D Knight Rider / K.I.T.T. game, requested "by unity engine", as a playable OMGithub web project with a matching Unity project included.

## Requirements
- User explicitly requested a 3D Knight Rider game made with Unity engine.
- Working environment serves a browser app on port 3002; Unity editor is unavailable, so a Three.js playable version is being built alongside a hand-authored Unity project.
- Support desktop and mobile browser gameplay with responsive UI/touch controls.
- Do not use the copyrighted Knight Rider theme; synth audio must be original.
- Deliver both a polished browser-playable Three.js game and a Unity C#/scene project mirroring it.

## Decisions
- Use Vite + Three.js 0.169 with postprocessing bloom, ACES tone mapping, procedural car/environment geometry (no external models), canvas-generated textures, and synthesized WebAudio music/SFX.
- KITT is procedurally built from lofted geometry with red scanner, gold pinstripes, T-tops, louvers, taillights, spoiler, spoke wheels, headlights/spotlights and license plate.
- Gameplay: endless neon Nevada highway pursuit — collect data cores (+time), laser interceptors, dodge traffic, near-miss combo scoring, turbo boost, ramps/jumps, 120s timer, shields, rank/debrief.
- Unity deliverable is source-only; actual Unity editor/WebGL build cannot be produced here.
- Unity project will proceduralize everything at runtime and use a single bootstrap scene with `GameBootstrap` MonoBehaviour; Unity scripts reference Standard shader via a committed base material to avoid build shader stripping.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created Vite/Three.js project and installed dependencies.
- Built full HUD/title/pause/game-over/mobile-control DOM and 80s neon CSS, including Orbitron/Rajdhani fonts.
- Implemented procedural KITT, traffic cars, interceptors, data cores, ramps, particles/explosions/lasers.
- Implemented full browser game loop: driving, turbo, steering, jumping, collisions, near misses, lasers, scoring/combo, shields, timer, difficulty, chase camera/menu orbit camera, game-over ranks.
- Implemented synthesized engine audio, scanner ping, music sequencer, laser/crash/pickup/boost/jump/game-over SFX.
- Implemented world: scrolling road texture, guardrails, streetlights, gantries/signs, overpasses, cacti, rocks, mountains, city, stars, moon, title backdrop.
- Fixed NaN wedge geometry, speedometer ring masking, brake/tail glow orientation, stray title "3D", bloom blowouts, KITT body/cabin/wheels/lighting.
- Optimized wheel meshes using merged geometry and cached wheel assets: scene meshes reduced from 2003 to 640.
- Added rear hatch louvers, quarter glass, slimmer spoiler, reduced underglow; further reduced headlight spotlight/bloom intensity to 5.2.
- Fixed game-over distance display (was raw world units, now divided by 1609.34).
- Added `?touch=1` query override for touch layout testing.
- Fixed mobile landscape HUD overlap: `.hud-right` moved below score; touch controls repositioned to mid-screen at `top: 46%`.
- Verified browser gameplay: start, driving, turbo, firing/kills, core pickup, collision damage, ramp jump, pause/resume, time-expiry game-over/restart.
- Captured desktop, mobile portrait, mobile landscape, touch, gameplay, and game-over screenshots.
- `npm run build` succeeds.
- Created Unity project skeleton and converted web fonts to TTF under Unity `Resources/Fonts`.
- Wrote Unity scripts: `MeshUtils`, `RuntimeAssets`, `KittCar`, `VehicleFactory`, `WorldBuilder`, `ChaseCamera`, `SynthAudio`, `FxManager`, `GameManager`.

### Active
- Unity project still needs its `Hud.cs`, `GameBootstrap.cs`, scene YAML, `.meta` files, project settings, package manifest, and in-project README.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.
